name: CardioSyntax
description: The SYNTAX score has become a widely used measure of coronary disease severity, crucial in selecting the optimal mode of the revascularization procedure. This paper introduces a new medical regression and classification problem - automatically estimating SYNTAX score from coronary angiography. Our study presents a comprehensive CardioSYNTAX dataset of 3,018 patients for the SYNTAX score estimation and coronary dominance classification. The dataset features a balanced distribution of individuals with zero and non-zero scores. This dataset includes a first-of-its-kind, complete coronary angiography samples captured through a multi-view X-ray video, allowing one to observe coronary arteries from multiple perspectives. Furthermore, we present a novel, fully automatic end-to-end method for estimating the SYNTAX. For such a difficult task, we have achieved a solid coefficient of determination R2 of 0.51 in score value prediction and 77.3% accuracy for zero score classification.
evaluation_method: Regression: R^2, MAE, RMSE; Classification: accuracy and AUC
general_score_metric: R^2 for SYNTAX score regression; accuracy for zero/non-zero classification
typical_sota_score: R^2 ≈ 0.51 (regression reported by authors); accuracy ≈ 77.3% (zero-score classification)
reputation: A new, specialized medical-imaging dataset proposed for automated SYNTAX score estimation and coronary dominance classification; important for research but currently limited adoption outside the authors' work.
notes: Moderate-sized clinical dataset (≈3,000 patients) with multi-view X-ray video — sensitive medical data with potential label noise and inter-rater variability; requires clinical expertise to interpret and is not an LLM benchmark.
